questions.question: What protocol encrypts web traffic?
questions.explanation: HTTPS secures data with encryption.

questions.question: What attack injects malicious scripts?
questions.explanation: XSS executes scripts in victim browsers.

questions.question: What attack injects malicious database queries?
questions.explanation: SQL injection manipulates database queries.

questions.question: What certificate validates website identity?
questions.explanation: SSL certificates verify site authenticity.

questions.question: What verifies user credentials?
questions.explanation: Authentication confirms user identity.

questions.question: What attack overwhelms servers with traffic?
questions.explanation: DDoS floods servers with requests.

questions.question: What policy controls resource access?
questions.explanation: CORS manages cross-origin requests.

questions.question: What firewall protects web applications?
questions.explanation: WAF filters HTTP traffic to applications.

questions.question: What prevents automated bot attacks?
questions.explanation: CAPTCHA distinguishes humans from bots.

questions.question: What stores encrypted passwords?
questions.explanation: Hashing transforms passwords irreversibly.

questions.question: What attack uses fake emails or websites to steal credentials?
questions.explanation: Phishing deceives users into revealing sensitive data.

questions.question: What malware encrypts victim files until a payment is made?
questions.explanation: Ransomware holds data hostage for payment.

questions.question: What attack tries many password combinations systematically?
questions.explanation: Brute force attempts every possible credential combination.

questions.question: What attack steals a user's active session token to impersonate them?
questions.explanation: Hijacking reuses stolen session identifiers.

questions.question: What secret value embedded in forms blocks forged cross-site requests?
questions.explanation: CSRF tokens prove requests originate from the real site.

questions.question: What defense converts special characters to safe text before rendering?
questions.explanation: Encoding output prevents injected markup from executing.

questions.question: Which cookie attribute prevents JavaScript from reading it?
questions.explanation: HttpOnly blocks client-side script access to cookies.

questions.question: Which cookie attribute sends it only over HTTPS connections?
questions.explanation: Secure cookies transmit only on encrypted connections.

questions.question: Which cookie attribute controls whether it is sent on cross-site requests?
questions.explanation: SameSite restricts cookies on cross-origin requests.

questions.question: What technique limits repeated login attempts from one source?
questions.explanation: Rate limiting slows brute-force and abuse attempts.

questions.question: What random value added to passwords before hashing defeats rainbow tables?
questions.explanation: Salts make each hash unique per password.

questions.question: What database technique safely embeds user input into queries?
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate code from data.

questions.question: What XSS type permanently stores malicious script in a database?
questions.explanation: Stored XSS persists scripts in server data.

questions.question: What XSS type reflects the script back immediately from a request?
questions.explanation: Reflected XSS bounces payloads off the response.

questions.question: An attacker overlays an invisible iframe of a bank page on a fake button. What attack is this?
questions.explanation: Clickjacking tricks users into hidden-frame clicks.

questions.question: An attacker forces a known session ID on a victim before login. What attack is this?
questions.explanation: Fixation sets the session ID before authentication.
